key_insight: DualG-MRAG separates high-level reasoning from low-level retrieval matching, making multimodal RAG better at complex multi-hop tasks. The core idea is to avoid bloated graphs by decoupling macro-reasoning over relationships from micro-matching over fine-grained visual and text cues.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the weakness of current multimodal retrieval-augmented generation systems on complex multi-hop reasoning. Existing methods often rely on instance-level matching or graph expansion that becomes inefficient and noisy when fine-grained visual features are included.
method: Decouple multimodal reasoning into two stages: macro-reasoning for global relational structure and micro-matching for local evidence alignment.
Use structured reasoning to capture explicit relationships across documents and modalities without forcing every fine-grained feature into one large graph.
Improve retrieval and generation for complex queries by balancing semantic structure with detailed visual/textual matching.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more scalable and accurate way to build multimodal RAG systems for tasks requiring multi-hop reasoning. It is especially useful when documents include both text and images, where naive graph construction can become too large and difficult to optimize.

paper_title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
